videos.caption: SINGLE-SERVE HEALTHY BROWNIE. The ultimate chocolate fix that actually supports your cycle.🍫 If you find yourself craving something chocolatey at the end of your cycle, let me introduce you to my Single-Serve Healthy Brownie. I originally created this for a VVIP client back in my personal chef days to satisfy her sweet tooth, whilst giving her a much-needed boost of magnesium + iron - two essentials our bodies crave most during that window. This is professional-grade comfort that actually supports your body. It satisfies those cravings without the blood sugar spike. High-integrity, refined sugar-free, + zero compromise. THE INGREDIENTS 35 g organic grass-fed butter 80 g + 30 g 85% dark chocolate, chopped 1 organic pasture-raised egg 55 g coconut blossom sugar 1/4 teaspoon pure vanilla extract 1/8 teaspoon Celtic sea salt 35 g organic cassava flour THE METHOD Prepare the Base: Preheat your oven to 180°C + grease a small oven-proof dish with parchment paper. Melt the Chocolate: Using a bain-marie (a heat-proof bowl over a pot of simmering water), gently melt the butter + 80g of the dark chocolate together until glossy + smooth. Whisk for Texture: In a separate bowl, whisk the egg + coconut blossom sugar until the mixture is pale, frothy, + the sugar has fully dissolved. Combine the Flavours: Stir the vanilla through the egg mixture, then slowly whisk in the warm melted chocolate until the batter looks smooth + chocolatey. Fold + Incorporate: Gently fold in the cassava flour + sea salt using a spatula until just combined, then stir through the remaining 30g of chocolate chunks. Bake to Perfection: Pour the batter into your lined dish + bake for 22 minutes. Allow the brownie to cool completely at room temperature so the centre sets into a fudgy texture. SAVE this for when the craving hits - your body will thank-you later. Which team are you: fudgy centre or chewy edges? 👇

The Hershey Chocolate Explanation: Most people know the chocolate. Few know the struggle behind Milton S. Hershey. Before success, he failed repeatedly. In the late 1800s, his candy businesses in Philadelphia, Chicago, and New York all collapsed. He returned home broke, with bad credit and a reputation as a failure. But he didn’t stop. In 1886, he built the Lancaster Caramel Company using fresh milk, and it became a global success. Then came his biggest risk. After seeing chocolate machinery in 1893, he sold his entire caramel business in 1900 and bet everything on milk chocolate. It worked. He built a factory, a town, and a brand that changed the industry forever. His story proves one thing — failure isn’t the end. It’s often the beginning.
